historical_claims.anchor: Georges Humbert had been Jordan's student
Three of Jordan's six sons died during World War I
Jordan began examining students at the École Polytechnique in eighteen seventy-three
He was elected to the Académie des Sciences in eighteen eighty-one and served as president of the Société Mathématique de France in eighteen eighty.
In eighteen eighty-five he became editor of the Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées
Jordan retired from his official teaching positions in nineteen twelve.
